 Follow No frigid air coming to US in November despite polar vortex being on the move
 Alex Sosnowski Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:13 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. AccuWeather.com An evolving shift in the polar vortex is on the way, but it does not necessarily mean frigid air is coming for the United States.
 October was an incredibly warm month for much of the northern half of the nation. It was also largely dry in the East, except for parts of Florida and the Gulf Coast.
 "The jet stream is going to develop some big buckles over the Northern Hemisphere over the next couple of weeks, which would normally allow the frigid air to travel southward," AccuWeather Meteorologist Alex DaSilva said. The jet stream surrounds the globe and is a high-speed ribbon of air at the altitude where jets fly.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A strong polar vortex tends to keep frigid air locked up near the Arctic Circle, but when it weakens, as is expected into November, cold air can move southward.
 However, there is one big problem with the polar vortex event this time -the air in northern Canada is not all that cold to begin with.
 Temperatures will trend lower in parts of the U.S. later during the first and second weeks of November. That change will be more due to slow homegrown chilly air from large jet stream storms forming overhead, rather than a bitterly cold blast that will race thousands of miles from the Arctic Circle.
 "This time, what true cold air exists in the pattern will be directed to Siberia, rather than North America," AccuWeather Senior Meteorologist Brett Anderson said.
 Some of the biggest temperature dips during the first half of November will tend to skip over the Northern states and evolve over the Southwest in response to a large storm in the jet stream, Anderson explained.
 The biggest change in the pattern that should become noticeable to just about everyone in the eastern half of the nation will be an end to the weeks-long sunny days with warm afternoons. This stretch is probably more unusual for so long for so many areas than the upcoming cooler weather with some rain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Like in the Southwest, a large storm at the jet stream level of the atmosphere will help focus the rain and the cooler air.
 Multiple rainy days are ahead for much of the East during the first couple weeks of November, compared to the last two weeks of October. Wet conditions will persist in the Southwest and expand over the South Central states.
 The pattern may cool a bit more during the second half of November.
 "The blocking pattern in the jet stream may break down enough to allow some chillier air episodes to move southward into the U.S. during the latter part of November and December," AccuWeather Senior Long-Range Meteorologist Joe Lundberg said.
 It could still be a challenge for some ski resorts open for Thanksgiving in the East, as there may be a lack of snow and especially cold air to make their own snow, Lundberg added.
